instagram_reel.script:
I found a rosé at the LCBO that wine people get a little excited about: Domaine Maby La Forcadière Tavel Rosé 2025.

Tavel comes from the southern Rhône, and it’s known for making rosé only. This style is deeper in colour, more structured, and way more food-friendly than a lot of the pale pink bottles people reach for.

This one has cranberry and cherry fruit, a little spice, fresh acidity, and a savoury edge. So yes, it works with salmon or shrimp, but it can also handle roast chicken, charcuterie, and even ribs.

It’s $24.95 at the LCBO, and it’s one I’d happily bring to the table.

linkedin.post:
One of the easiest ways to show people that wine can be welcoming is to meet them where they already are. Rosé is a perfect example.

Domaine Maby La Forcadière Tavel Rosé 2025 is a great reminder that rosé has range. Tavel is a small appellation in the southern Rhône devoted to rosé production, and this style brings more colour, more texture, and more food-pairing flexibility than many people expect.

What stands out here is structure. That matters when a wine needs to work with salmon, shrimp, roast chicken, charcuterie, or richer dishes like ribs. It also makes the wine feel more substantial at the table, which is part of why Tavel has such a loyal following.

For retail shelves, this is the kind of bottle that can help reset expectations. It offers an approachable entry point, but it also rewards a drinker who wants to go a little deeper on style and region.

At $24.95 at the LCBO, it’s a smart bottle to know about and an easy one to recommend.
